task: This is a synthetic writing exercise. Using these fictional reporting notes, write a newspaper news story for general readers. Draw only on the supplied notes; do not invent additional reported events, scenes, or quotations. Write from this reporting snapshot as of November 14, 2024. Include a headline. Target 450 to 650 words. Follow AP style.

facts.text: The Federal Energy Licensing Commission voted 4–1 on November 14, 2024, to grant a construction permit to Meridian Fusion Sciences for a commercial fusion power plant in Reston Flats, Wyoming.
The permit is the first ever issued for a commercial fusion facility in the United States.
Meridian's proposed plant, called the Reston Fusion Station, is designed to generate 400 megawatts of net electrical output.
The safety review spanned 38 months and examined neutron activation of structural materials, tritium handling, and electromagnetic confinement failure scenarios.
The Commission determined fusion reactions produce no chain-reaction risk and that the facility's primary radiological hazard is tritium, a mildly radioactive hydrogen isotope.
Construction is expected to take seven years; Meridian projects first power generation by 2032 at the earliest.
The plant would use a tokamak design and require a continuous supply of deuterium and tritium fuel; tritium will be bred on-site from lithium blankets.

Meridian Fusion Sciences CEO Dr. Sanjay Parikh said: "This permit represents the most rigorous safety evaluation ever conducted for a fusion facility, and we intend to meet every condition attached to it."

Commission Chair Elena Voronova said the vote reflected the agency's finding that fusion's hazard profile differs fundamentally from fission and that existing nuclear regulations required substantial adaptation to apply.
The dissenting commissioner cited insufficient public comment time on the tritium storage plan, which was revised 11 months into the review.

Nuclear policy researcher Dr. Marcus Webb of the Clearwater Energy Institute said: "Approval-stage optimism has historically outpaced operational performance in first-of-kind energy facilities. The timeline risk here is real."
Meridian has raised $4.1 billion in private investment and has a conditional $1.3 billion loan guarantee from the Department of Energy pending construction milestones.
Wyoming's governor welcomed the permit, citing an estimated 2,400 construction jobs and 180 permanent operations positions.
Two environmental groups filed for administrative review within hours of the vote, arguing the tritium storage environmental impact statement was inadequate.
The permit requires Meridian to submit quarterly construction reports and grants the Commission authority to halt work if safety benchmarks are not met.
Fusion reactions combine light hydrogen isotopes rather than split heavy atoms, producing no long-lived radioactive waste of the kind generated by fission reactors.
Global fusion investment has exceeded $6 billion in private capital since 2020, with more than 30 companies pursuing commercial timelines, according to the Fusion Industry Association.
The Commission has not yet issued guidance on how future fusion plant operators should handle end-of-life decommissioning of activated structural components.
The Reston Flats site was selected partly for its remote location and access to Wyoming's existing high-voltage transmission infrastructure.
No fusion plant anywhere in the world has yet operated at net positive energy output on a sustained commercial basis.
